name: RemovableChip
purpose: A value the reader has already chosen, with a named way to take it back.
notFor: A filter that toggles on and off. That is FilterChip — and the two are separate components because the remove button's name is not the chip's text, which is a difference that would otherwise land in the accessibility tree.
A fact about the row. That is Badge.
A list needing reorder or bulk selection. That is ListView.
A destructive removal that needs confirming. Confirm it in the form around the chip, not inside it.

anatomy.note: Also carries bh-chip--removable. Not interactive: only the remove button is, so there is one tab stop per chip.
24 x 24 CSS pixels, the WCAG 2.5.8 minimum target. Sizing it to the glyph is the usual mistake.

label.meaning: The visible text, and the stem of the remove button's name.

onRemove.meaning: Fired when the remove button is activated.

removeLabel.note: Defaults to `Remove {label}`. Pass it when the label is a bare noun: "Remove Finance" reads like removing the department. What it must never be is the glyph — eight chips then announce as eight identical buttons, and the reader has to leave each one to find out what it does.

keyboard.Tab: Moves focus to the remove button. The chip itself is not a tab stop.

aria.role: button (on bh-chip__remove only; the chip itself carries no role, because it is text)
aria.labelling: The remove button is named by removeLabel, via aria-label, and names what it removes rather than the action alone. The glyph inside it is aria-hidden, so the name is never "multiplication sign".
aria.focus: Ring from bh-focusable on the remove button. Removing the last chip leaves focus where the button was, so the surrounding container must render something rather than nothing — an empty container is indistinguishable from a broken one.
aria.announcements: None. Removal is immediate and visible; a live region announcing every removed tag would speak over a reader clearing several.

attributes.aria-hidden: on the glyph inside the remove button

content.removeLabel: Verb, then the kind of thing, then its name: "Remove tag Finance". Sentence case, no trailing period.
